title: intent at edit --kind resets a row to to-write and drops its verdict in silence, where its help says it refuses a status the new kind cannot hold
body:
Found on 2026-09-24 by vc's working-with-llms subagent in the 3.2.1 doc audit, and driven by vc in a scratch project on the pair at `4c687eaad`.

Seen: a non-test acceptance test at `n/a` (after `intent at na`), re-kinded with `intent at edit ST0001 AT-01.1 --kind test`, exits 0 with "ok: AT-01.1 re-cited", and `intent at list` then shows the row at `to-write`: its verdict is gone, and nothing said so. `intent at edit --help` describes `--kind` as "Re-kind the row: test or non-test -- refused if the row's status cannot hold it". A test row cannot hold `n/a`, and the edit was not refused; the row was restarted at the new kind's entry state.

Expected: re-kinding a row that holds a verdict either refuses, as the help says, or says that it reset the verdict and to what.

Disposition: vc, 2026-09-24 -- filed for after the stabilisation line. `docs/concepts/criteria-and-tests.md` and `intent/docs/working-with-llms.md` state the as-built behaviour.
